teams.heading: Steve Borthwick secures Premiership refereeing overhaul to boost England World Cup hopes
teams.body: The Premiership has agreed to revamp its refereeing interpretations for the upcoming season to align more closely with the international game, directly aiding England head coach Steve Borthwick's preparations for next year's World Cup in Australia. Areas of focus include the offside line, the scrum's brake-foot law, and the breakdown — areas Borthwick previously flagged as inconsistent compared to elite Test levels. Following a presentation by the Rugby Football Union's refereeing team, Premiership directors of rugby agreed to these changes to help close the gap.

lead.why: The Premiership's refereeing overhaul directly addresses Steve Borthwick's concerns about domestic standards ahead of the World Cup.

teams.heading: Ireland Under-20 star Noah Byrne rejects Leinster to join AFL
teams.body: Emerging full-back Noah Byrne has opted to exit the Irish rugby system, rejecting a professional academy contract with Leinster to sign with the Brisbane Lions. The 20-year-old was a standout performer during this year's Under-20 Six Nations, starting every match for Andrew Browne’s side. Recognised for his significant pace and playmaking ability, Byrne’s transition to the Australian Football League marks a notable loss for the Leinster academy as they look to develop the next generation of domestic talent.

teams.heading: Italy Men To Host Reigning World Champions South Africa In Turin
teams.body: International rugby returns to the Allianz Stadium this November as Italy prepare to host South Africa in the Nations Championship. Following away fixtures against Japan, New Zealand, and Australia, this clash serves as the Azzurri's first home fixture in the new competition. The fixture was officially presented at the stadium last weekend, highlighting the ongoing partnership between the Italian Rugby Federation and local institutions. Gonzalo Quesada’s side will be looking to capitalise on home support before continuing their autumn series.

teams.heading: Scotland winger Darcy Graham ruled out of the upcoming autumn tests
teams.body: Scotland have been dealt a major setback as record try-scorer Darcy Graham faces at least 12 weeks on the sidelines. The Edinburgh winger sustained a ruptured bicep during a collision in a friendly match last week. Edinburgh head coach Sean Everitt confirmed the news, stating, "That's not good news for us and not good news for him, especially with the autumn series coming up." Graham will now miss the upcoming fixtures against New Zealand, Australia and Japan.

lead.why: The injury to Scotland's record try-scorer is the most significant news regarding the men's senior national team today.

teams.heading: Dewi Lake And Jac Morgan Prepare For Gloucester Premiership Debuts
teams.body: Former Wales co-captains Dewi Lake and Jac Morgan are preparing to make their Premiership debuts for Gloucester against Exeter after completing their moves from the Ospreys. Lake has been unveiled as the new Gloucester captain with Morgan named as one of his deputies following their high-profile departures from Welsh rugby. The pair, who have been almost inseparable since meeting a decade ago, admitted they texted each other before their first day at the club to coordinate their arrival in the car park.

teams.heading: Pumas Power Past Iberians With Ten-Try Display in Tbilisi
teams.body: Argentina's Pumas recorded an emphatic 64-21 victory over Spain's Iberians in Tbilisi, holding a commanding 40-14 lead at half-time. Left wing Tino Swanepoel delivered a standout performance by crossing five times during the 10-try rout. Clinton Swart, Wian van Niekerk, Gustav du Rand, Alfondso Isaacs and André Fouché also touched down, with Swart adding 5 conversions alongside 2 from Bradley Giddy.

teams.heading: Les Kiss considers shifting Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to wing against Springboks
teams.body: Wallabies coach Les Kiss is reportedly preparing to redeploy Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to the wing for Sunday's Test against the Springboks in Perth, marking the first time the 24-Test star will start outside the midfield. The planned positional switch, first reported by the Sydney Morning Herald, is designed to harness the 23-year-old's aerial athleticism against South Africa's formidable kicking game. The expected backline reshuffle should see Hunter Paisami slot into inside centre while Len Ikitau returns to his favoured No 13 jersey.

teams.heading: Japan edge Fiji to claim Pacific Nations Cup title at Chichibunomiya
teams.body: The Brave Blossoms secured their first Pacific Nations Cup title since 2019 with a hard-fought 20-15 victory over Fiji at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium. Mamoru Harada crossed for a first-half try before Ben Gunter powered over after the break to help overturn a half-time deficit. Captain Naoto Saito reflected on the milestone, saying, "It's a great breakthrough to create history for Japan. It gives this young team great confidence." The triumph lifts the team to ninth in the World Rugby rankings.

lead.why: Japan won the Pacific Nations Cup by defeating Fiji 20-15.

teams.heading: Scott Barrett set for long-awaited rugby return with Taranaki
teams.body: Former All Blacks captain Scott Barrett is back to full fitness and will make his long-awaited return from a back injury by starting at lock for Taranaki against Hawke's Bay in Napier on Sunday. Barrett has been sidelined for the entire season after undergoing surgery for a bulging disc that depowered his left side and ruled him out of the Greatest Rivalry series. Reflecting on a challenging 10 months following the coaching transition from Scott Robertson to Dave Rennie, Barrett admitted it was difficult but confirmed he has spoken with Rennie regarding the captaincy change to Ardie Savea.

lead.why: Scott Barrett is returning from a long-term back injury in the NPC.

teams.heading: Andre Esterhuizen Captains Rotated Springboks Side For Wallabies Test Clash
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has named Andre Esterhuizen as captain in an overhauled Springboks starting XV featuring 13 changes for Sunday's one-off Test against Australia in Perth. Only lock Eben Etzebeth and winger Ethan Hooker are retained in the run-on side from the win over New Zealand in Baltimore. Erasmus explained the rotation provides security with an experienced bench featuring Jasper Wiese, who is set to earn his 50th cap among the replacements.
